summary: Kshitimohan Sen worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning an M.A. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University around 1902–1904. He held posts with the Chamba State Department of Education (c. 1907–1908) and Visva-Bharati University, serving as Adhyaksha in 1953–1954.
Kumar Shrestha is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. In 2018, he was attested in posts at the National Archives of Nepal and on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.

Kumataro Kawada worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning degrees including a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University (1927), Tokyo University of Literature and Science (1943), the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).
Kumja Paik Kim is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate from Stanford University and became curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum in 1989.

Kumkum Bandyopadhyay is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay. As of 2026, she is attested as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Kun Chang specialized in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology, studying at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He held positions at Academia Sinica (c. 1940–1947), the University of Washington (1951), and the University of California, Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a BA and PhD degrees at Kyushu University, studying under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara. He held faculty posts at Saga University (c. 1978–1988) and Saga Medical School (c. 1988–1993).
Kunio Iwaya studied at the University of Tokyo around 1963–1969. He subsequently held a post at Meiji Gakuin University from approximately 1970 to 2014.

Kunio Mugitani is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga between 1971 and 1976. He served as a professor at Kyoto University from approximately 1994 to 2012.
Kunio Odaka studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1928 to 1931. He later held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (c. 1943–1969) and Sophia University (c. 1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita worked in Japanology and religious studies, having studied law at the University of Tokyo. His career included roles in the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, Privy Council, Keio University, and Kokugakuin University.

Kuno Fischer was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg between 1844 and 1847. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University (c. 1850–1906) and the University of Jena (c. 1856–1872).

Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, Kiel (PhD), and Erlangen-Nuremberg (Habilitation). He held a chair in philosophy at the University of Hamburg in 1970 and served as professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

Kuno Meyer was a linguist who studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (c. 1879–1883). He held posts at the University of Liverpool (c. 1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (c. 1911–1915).

Kuntala Bhattacharya is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, and was attested in a post at Rabindra Bharati University in 2009.
Kunzang Namgyal was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Shenphen Nangwa, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. His students included Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
summary: Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).

Kurt A. Behrendt is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at UCLA. At the Metropolitan Museum of Art, he was Assistant Curator (c. 2007–2014) and became Associate Curator of South Asian Art (c. 2014).
Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar in Indology who completed his PhD at the University of York by 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.
